title: Decision Practice
subtitle: Stop & Decide prompts to build active clinical judgment
howToUse: These decision points interrupt passive reading and force active thinking. For each scenario, pause and write your response. Then compare with the model response. Focus on (1) the immediate risk, (2) the safest first nursing action, and (3) what data you must check next.

decisions.title: Chemical exposure
decisions.scenario: A hazardous chemical spills onto the floor in a treatment area. The substance produces a strong odor, and staff are unsure how to safely manage the spill.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Isolate the area and follow spill protocol.

decisions.title: Pressure injury prevention
decisions.scenario: An immobile patient who spends most of the day in bed is noted to have redness over the sacral area. The skin is intact but warm and tender to touch.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Reposition the patient and protect skin.

decisions.title: Infection outbreak
decisions.scenario: Several patients on the unit develop vomiting and diarrhea within a short time frame. Staff notice a pattern of similar symptoms emerging across multiple rooms.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Notify infection control and implement precautions.

decisions.title: Bloodborne pathogen exposure
decisions.scenario: During a procedure, blood splashes into a nurse’s eyes. The nurse feels startled and experiences immediate discomfort but continues assisting with the procedure.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Flush eyes immediately and report exposure.

decisions.title: Safe patient identification
decisions.scenario: A patient scheduled for a procedure is found without an identification band. The patient confirms their name verbally, but no formal identification is visible.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Verify identity and apply ID band.

decisions.title: Emergency preparedness
decisions.scenario: A sudden power outage occurs in the hospital. Lights go out briefly before emergency lighting activates, and several patients rely on electrically powered medical equipment.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

decisions.title: Food safety
decisions.scenario: A patient undergoing chemotherapy with severe neutropenia is served a meal containing raw fruit and unpasteurised food items. The patient begins eating the meal.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Remove food and provide safe alternatives.

decisions.title: Waste disposal
decisions.scenario: A staff member disposes of blood-contaminated materials into a regular trash bin instead of the designated biohazard container.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Correct the disposal and educate staff.
